newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Alumbrera says has talked to BHP project.
newsitem.headline: Alumbrera says has talked to BHP project.

text.p: Minera Alumbrera Ltd, a $900 million Australian-Canadian copper joint-venture, has said it has had early talks with Australia's Broken Hill Proprietary Ltd about sharing infrastructure.

"Yes, it's true but they are very preliminary," Alumbrera President Peter Freund told reporters late Tuesday, when asked by Reuters if talks had taken place on sharing infrastructure with BHP's nearby Agua Rica copper project.

Alumbrera's Bajo de la Alumbrera copper and gold mine is due to start up in August in Argentina's northwestern province of Catamarca. BHP has 70 percent of the Agua Rica prospect nearby, while Canadian firm Northern Orion is the junior partner.
Freund mentioned the possibity of pooling some power resources and said Alumbrera would agree to sharing infrastructure "if it is an economic prospect without increasing the risk to our project."
Alumbrera is held 50 percent by Australia's MIM Holdings Ltd. Australia's North Ltd and Canada's Rio Algom Ltd, each have 25 percent.
Alumbrera is set to produce 190,000 tonnes of copper in concentrates a year, plus 730,000 ounces of gold.
